capabilities.scope: Mosquitto TCP listener; automated qualification covers MQTT 3.1.1 and MQTT 5
one mounted password secret per policy principal
one explicit or compatibly inferred namespace per managed principal; default deny outside it
application principals are denied $SYS/# and $CONTROL/#; the health principal can read only an aggregate $SYS allow-list
TLS 1.2 or newer with separately mounted server and health-client identities

immutable identity generations, atomic current-pointer activation, durable interruption recovery, post-reload readiness, TLS candidate validation, payload-free audit, explicit revocation, and forced reauthentication by restart
stable service ID and broker-enforced username-derived client IDs; one bounded session identity per managed principal
broker-enforced listener connections/principal count, packet/payload bytes, inflight count/bytes, offline queue count/bytes, broker heap, keepalive, retained cleanup, and persistent-client age

curated aggregate $SYS metrics and readiness/storage diagnostics without client IDs, usernames, topic payloads, or secret values
single-node Mosquitto persistence with clean-stop restore qualification

capabilities.reason: No browser-facing broker listener is part of this platform-service contract.
Anonymous clients cannot be assigned a workload namespace and are rejected.
Requires an orchestrator and broker topology contract outside this single-container package.
The package documents coupled-state backup and tests restore; encryption and retention belong to platform storage orchestration.
Readiness enforces a free-space floor and procedures cover stop/restore; destructive disk-full and corrupt-database qualification remain operator-only.
Mosquitto 2.0 does not provide package-configured per-principal publish rate, bandwidth, live-session, or subscription-count quotas.

The package tests a read-only root filesystem and a persistence free-space floor; CPU, container RSS, process/file-descriptor, volume capacity, and log-retention hard limits still require orchestrator enforcement.
A broker is protocol infrastructure; physical-device and field qualification are explicitly outside this release.
